import itertools

# Propositional encoding of the passage. Each variable is one claim.
VARS = ["Sub", "S", "Dis", "Endure", "Obj", "Hard", "DivEra", "Alive", "Unan", "Great"]

def imp(a, b):
    return (not a) or b

def premises(m, bridge):
    # Textual premises
    p = [
        m["Sub"],                        # aesthetic judgment is subjective in a short period
        m["S"],                          # contemporary evaluations diverge greatly
        m["Dis"],                        # over time subjectivity disappears (evaluations converge)
        imp(m["Endure"], m["Obj"]),      # long-enduring works can be called great objectively
        imp(m["Dis"], not m["DivEra"]),  # convergence over time => no large cross-era divergence
    ]
    # Interpretive bridge (NOT stated verbatim): short-period subjectivity applies to
    # contemporary works and therefore makes their value hard to fix objectively.
    if bridge:
        p.append(imp(m["Sub"], m["Hard"]))
    return all(p)

# Options, each as the content of the statement
OPTIONS = {
    "A": lambda m: m["Alive"],                 # evaluations of Da Vinci/Bach differed while alive
    "B": lambda m: m["Hard"],                  # contemporary value is hard to determine objectively
    "C": lambda m: m["DivEra"],                # same work evaluated very differently across eras
    "D": lambda m: imp(m["Unan"], m["Great"]), # unanimous critical affirmation => great work
}

models = [dict(zip(VARS, vals))
          for vals in itertools.product([False, True], repeat=len(VARS))]

def classify(bridge):
    sat = [m for m in models if premises(m, bridge)]
    status = {}
    for name, fn in OPTIONS.items():
        vals = [bool(fn(m)) for m in sat]
        if not sat:
            status[name] = "NO MODELS"
        elif all(vals):
            status[name] = "ENTAILED"
        elif not any(vals):
            status[name] = "CONTRADICTED"
        else:
            status[name] = "NEITHER"
    return len(sat), status

n_text, st_text = classify(bridge=False)
n_bridge, st_bridge = classify(bridge=True)

print(f"Models satisfying textual premises only: {n_text}")
for k in sorted(st_text):
    print(f"  text-only  {k}: {st_text[k]}")
print(f"Models satisfying premises + bridge: {n_bridge}")
for k in sorted(st_bridge):
    print(f"  with bridge {k}: {st_bridge[k]}")

submitted = "B"
entailed = [k for k, v in st_bridge.items() if v == "ENTAILED"]
contradicted = [k for k, v in st_bridge.items() if v == "CONTRADICTED"]
print(f"Entailed options (with bridge): {entailed}")
print(f"Contradicted options: {contradicted}")
print(f"Submitted answer: {submitted}")

if n_bridge == 0:
    print("CHECK UNKNOWN: premise set has no models")
elif entailed == [submitted] and st_bridge["C"] == "CONTRADICTED" and st_bridge["A"] == "NEITHER":
    print("CHECK PASS: B is the only option entailed under the stated reading; C is contradicted; A is unsupported.")
else:
    print("CHECK FAIL: submitted answer is not the unique entailed option under this encoding.")

print("UNSUPPORTED: the bridge premise is interpretive, not stated in the passage. "
      "Without it, no option is strictly entailed, so B rests on the reading that short-period subjectivity makes contemporary valuation hard.")
